First reconstruction, 2026-09-06: the whole body is transcribed and the candidate is stored in notes/overlays/candidates.md. It builds 499 of 495 instructions at opcode distance 32 under gcc_2_8_1_g0_split, with the frame, the saved-register set and the prologue order all exactly the target's - -0x28 with s0 through s4 and ra, and no s5. The one lever that mattered is the loop form. GCC 2.8.1 with -msplit-addresses hoists the %hi of any global read inside a for or while loop into a callee-saved register, which the target does not do: it rematerialises %hi(gMain_bMenuID) at both reads inside the entry loop. Writing the loop with an explicit goto instead removes the hoist entirely, because GCC 2.8's loop optimiser only sees loops the front end marked with loop notes. That single change took the frame from -0x30 with s5 to the target's -0x28 with s0-s4. It is recorded as a general lever in notes/research/matching-evidence.md. Measured and not helping: the same body with a for loop reaches exactly 495 instructions at distance 36, but with a 0x30 frame and six saved registers, so the count parity there is an artifact of two extra prologue instructions cancelling two saved lui - check the saved-register set before trusting a count match. name: func_80181728
notes: Exact boundary from the verified overlay split. Mapped but not matched; best candidate builds 352 of 356 instructions. The digit loops call MainMenu_CountDecimalDigits twice, once with 8000 to get the field width and once with the value to get the digit count, and step the value down by ten a digit. Levers confirmed. The marker's x is a conditional expression written as a test for the toggle being zero with 0x74 first, not as a test for it being non-zero; the polarity decides which constant lands in the branch delay slot. The digit x must come from an explicit walking offset that starts at -0x7E and gains 8 a pass rather than from an index expression: written as base minus i times 8 minus 0x7E, GCC re-associates it to base plus 0x7E minus i times 8 and recomputes the shift every iteration, which builds 346, while the walking form reproduces the target's induction variable and builds 352. What remains is four instructions and it is the four-invariant hoisting limit already recorded for func_801821DC's cohort. The target hoists exactly four loop invariants into callee-saved registers, the constants 0x6A 0x72 0x70 and 0x78, and is then out of budget, so it re-materialises the address of D_800E9D90 inside both loops at three instructions a pass. The candidate hoists that address instead, spending one instruction a pass, which is two per loop and four across the two loops. The same pressure difference is why the candidate spills the second display value to the frame at entry while the target keeps both in callee-saved registers and saves ten of them against the candidate's nine. No candidate for this function survives, so it was rebuilt from the disassembly starting with a prefix probe of the marker and the two side blocks. That probe reproduces target instructions 19 through 106 exactly, which is 88 instructions covering everything before the quads and the digit runs, so those spellings are now shape-verified rather than described. The marker is D_801845B0[2] and its x is the conditional already recorded, written as the toggle being zero with 116 first and 220 second, with y 74. Each side then reads its widget from D_801845B0 at index 0 or 1 and tests a short-circuit or: the busy word at +0x24 being non-zero, or the toggle byte at D_801845BC for that side being 2. On the true side it sets bit 0x40 of the halfword at +8, re-reads the widget pointer, and only when the busy word is zero writes the bar position and the y, which is 111 for the first side and 139 for the second. Row 0 holds a count in [0][0] and up to ten entries after it and row 1 the same at +0x16. That single declaration produces the whole shape of both loops. Written flat as D_80185C9C[11 + i + 1] GCC strength reduces the second loop into a walking byte offset and needs an extra register; written as D_80185C9C[1][i + 1] it recomputes the element address from i + 1 each iteration and reuses one materialised base for both the count at 0x16 and the elements, which is exactly the target. The first loop keeps the %hi register for the folded count at offset 0 and a separate materialised base for the elements, which is why it needs six callee-saved registers against the second loop's five. The loop bound is re-read every iteration and the index into the row is i + 1 because entry 0 is the count. The prologue is also solved: the 0x38 frame with both object pointers written to 0x10 and 0x14 of the stack before the first branch is what an aggregate local produces, either u8 *o[2] or a two field struct. Plain locals build a 0x30 frame and keep both pointers in callee-saved registers, and spelling D_801845EC[0] at every use builds a 0x30 frame and re-reads the global rather than the stack. What remains is one CSE behaviour worth 54 instructions. The target reloads the object pointer once per occurrence, so the three chained stores of 0x40 take three separate lw from the same stack slot into three registers, and each compound assignment takes two. Every aggregate spelling tried instead emits one load and reuses it, and with the pointer in a register GCC also fuses the two range tests into a single subtract and unsigned compare where the target reloads and branches twice. Measured and ruled out: plain locals; a local array; a local struct; the global element spelled at every use; and a static helper taking u8 ** which GCC 2.8.1 does not inline at -O2 so it emits real calls. Matched exactly. Three levers, and none of them work alone. The two object pointers are an aggregate local declared volatile, u8 *volatile o[2], which is what forces the 0x38 frame with both pointers at 0x10 and 0x14 of the stack and, more importantly, makes every occurrence reload from that slot instead of being common subexpression eliminated; that single qualifier is worth the 54 instructions the earlier candidate was missing. It also explains the unfilled load delay slots through the whole first half, because the scheduler may not move anything across a volatile access, while the two loops that touch no volatile object are scheduled normally. The three colour bytes are one chained assignment o[0][0xC] = o[0][0xD] = o[0][0xE] = 0x40, which evaluates the three addresses left to right and then stores right to left, exactly the observed order. The sign flip is a compound assignment, *(s16 *)(o[0] + 0x60) *= -1, so the address is evaluated once and the load is lh; written out as x = -x it evaluates the address twice and loads lhu. The range test is two differently signed reads of the same byte, an unsigned compare against 0x41 and a signed test for negative, which is what gives lbu with sltiu followed by lb with bgez. In the loops the coordinates must be spelled inline in the call arguments rather than assigned to locals first: identical instruction counts either way, but locals make the coordinate pseudos lose the callee-saved priority contest, giving s0 to the element address and s3 to x where the target has s0 to x and s2 to the element address.
